questions.question: Explain the concept of row binding in R using rbind().Also Create two data frames with identical column names representing sales data of two different months. Combine them using rbind() / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the concept of row binding in R using rbind().Also Create two data frames with
  • identical column names representing sales data of two different months. Combine them
  • using rbind() [U] / [CO2]
  • (Definition – 3 Marks; Key Points / Concept – 4 Marks; Syntax – 2 Marks; Example Creation
  • – 3 Marks; Combining using rbind() – 3 Marks)
  • Row binding is the process of combining data frames by adding rows one below another
  • using rbind().
  • It Combines rows, requires same column names and number of columns, and returns one
  • combined data frame.
  • Syntax: rbind(dataframe1, dataframe2)
  • Example Data Frames Creation:
  • jan <- data.frame(ProductID=c(1,2), Sales=c(5000,6000)); feb <- data.frame(ProductID=c(3,4),
  • Sales=c(5500,6500))
  • Combining Data Frames Using rbind():
  • total <- rbind(jan, feb)

questions.question: With suitable R code, explain how to create and customize a pie chart using base R. / [CO3] [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• With suitable R code, explain how to create and customize a pie chart using base R. [A] /
  • [CO3]
  • (Definition of Pie Chart – 3 Marks; Syntax of pie() – 2 Marks; Creating Data – 3 Marks;
  • Customizing (labels, colors, title) – 4 Marks; R Code / Output – 3 Marks)
  • A pie chart is a graphical representation that shows data as proportions of a whole.
  • Syntax : pie(x, labels, main, col)
  • Creating Data :
  • sales <- c(40, 30, 20, 10)
  • labels <- c("Product A", "Product B", "Product C", "Product D")
  • Customizing (labels, colors, title)
  • Labels name categories, colors improve appearance, and title describes the chart.
  • R Code / Output
  • pie(sales,
  • labels = labels,
  • main = "Sales Distribution",
  • col = c("red", "blue", "green", "yellow"))
